To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the back-to-back di-hadron spectra at high $p_{\rm T}$ are mainly produced by jets produced close and tangentially to the surface of dense matter; (2) a significant fraction of high $p_{T}$ dihadrons also originates from jets produced at medium center after losing finite amount energy; (3) the suppression factor of high $p_T $ dihadrons is more sensitive to the gluon density than single-hadron spectra, and therefore

the NLO pQDC parton model with modified fragmentation functions due to parton energy loss can explain the experimental data of high-$p_T$\ dihadron spectra and that high-$p_T$, back-to-back dihadrone spectra at the LHC are more robust than those at RHIC in probing the dense medium.

(i) the back-to-back dijet spectrum in p+p and p+A collisions is dominated by the jet production close and tangential (i.e., near the edge) to the dense medium; (ii) the suppression factor of high-$p_T$, back-to-back dijets is sensitive to the gluon density of the dense medium; and (iii) the dijet spectrum in A+A collisions is more robust than the single jet spectrum as a probe of the dense medium at LHC
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dihadron tomography of high-energy nuclear collisions within the NLO pQTD framework.

the study of the back-to-back dijet production at the LHC and RHIC energies within the next-to- leading order perturbative QCT parton model with energy loss incorporated via modified jet quenching fragmentation function.
the development and application of a theoretical framework to study the high $p_T$, high multiplicity, and back-to-back correlations in high-energy nuclear collisions in the NLO pQDC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NLO pQCT jet quenching model is in good agreement with the experimental data, and the extracted energy loss parameters are consistent with the previous studies in pQCD.
NLO pQcd calculations with energy loss can successfully describe the high $p_T$, high multiplicity data from the LHC.
NLO jet quenching model can describe the experimental data of both single hadron and dihadron production at both RHIC and LHC energies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NLO parton model calculations with jet quenchings incorporated are in good agreement with the experimental data on both the single and the back-to-back di-hadron spectra at RHIC and the LHC energies.
the dihadron spectra provide a more sensitive probe of the dense medium than the single hadrons.

NLO pQCT with medium-modified fragmentation functions can describe the high-$p_T$, large $R_{AA}$ hadron spectra in high energy heavy-ion collisions at the RHIC and LHC, but the extracted energy loss parameters $\Delta E_{jet}/E_0=0.3-0.4$ and $\lambda_{q,g} \sim 3-5$ fm are smaller than the ones from the single jet suppression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dihadron spectra at high $p_{T}$ can provide valuable information about the dense medium and the initial gluon distribution, which can not be obtained from the single hadron spectrum alone.
dihadron tomography is a powerful probe of the medium properties and jet quenching in high-energy nuclear collisions.
high $p_T$, high-multiplicity dihadron spectra are a sensitive probe of the dense matter produced in high-energy heavy ion collisions.
